After.description: What a hold's `after` waits for: another task to end, or a Linear issue to close.

Hold.description:
Why a task is held, and the conditions that release it once all of them hold. With none, a
person does.

after.description:
Other tasks' ids, or Linear issues such as `ENG-7`: until each task ends and each issue is
Done or Canceled. One value or a list.

blockers.description: Until the task's Linear issue has no open blocker.

if_closed.description: What a pull request closed without a merge does: `release`, `drop` or `ask`, the default.

merge.description:
Pull requests, `owner/name#42` or `42` in the task's repository: until each merges. One
value or a list.

reason.description: Why the task waits, shown to a person.

until.description: An RFC 3339 instant, or a duration such as `2 hours` after the hold.

Intervention.description: Who answers a task's asks. Unset, every ask goes to a person.

oneOf.description:
A person approves the plan: a grading step's result waits for an answer before the task
moves on, even for a green grade.

The trigger's `lead` answers asks in the person's place, except an ask whose answer lets an
irreversible step run and an ask whose answer runs a command.

Limits.description: Spend caps in dollars: per task, per local day and per week.

day.description: What may be spent in a local day.

week.description: What may be spent in a week from Monday 00:00 local time.

OnError.description: What a failed `pre` script does with its request.

oneOf.description: The request is published unchanged, with `pre.failed`.

OneOrMany_After.description: One value, or a list of them; null reads as none, as the single values it replaced did.

OneOrMany_string.description: One value, or a list of them; null reads as none, as the single values it replaced did.

Pre.description:
A trigger's `[pre]` script. Priory execs `argv` with no shell, writes the event and the request
as JSON on its stdin, and reads its decision from its exit and stdout.

argv.description: The command and its arguments. The first is an executable file inside the factory folder.

env.description:
Environment variables copied from the process that runs it, beside `PATH`, `LANG` and
`HOME`.

on_error.description:
What a script that fails does with the request: `pass` publishes it unchanged, `drop`
drops it. `pass` when unset.

timeout.description: How long it may run, at most `60s`; 10 seconds when unset.

description:
`triggers/<name>.toml` or `.yaml`: an event source, its filter and the workflow its events
start. The file name is the trigger's name.

at.description: The local time of day a schedule fires, `HH:MM`.

backfill.description: Whether the events of the first poll start tasks too.

caps.description: Spend caps in dollars for the trigger's tasks.

channel.description: The Slack channel id a `slack` trigger reads, such as `C0123`.

days.description: The weekdays a schedule fires on; every day when unset.

every.description: How often a schedule fires again after `at`, the same day; once a day when unset.

filter.description:
Values an event must have: `label` for GitHub; `team`, `project` (its name or id), `label`,
`state` for Linear; `text` for Slack.

hold.description: Files each task held, so it waits for a person or a condition before it starts.

intervention.description: Who answers its tasks' asks: `plan` or `hands-off`; a person when unset.

key.description: Which events are the same work, such as `issue.number`; for a schedule, a fixed key.

lane.description: The lane of its tasks, `<team>/<theme>`; `lanes.toml` derives it when unset.

lead.description:
The agent that answers asks of a `hands-off` task: a `claude-code` agent with a `shared`
session.

on.description: The event that starts a task, such as `issues.labeled`; depends on `source`.

pre.description:
A script of the factory that runs on each matching event before it becomes a task request,
and can drop the request or change it.

prompt.description: What a schedule's firing tells the task it wakes.

repo.description:
The repository the trigger's tasks work in, a GitHub `owner/name` with no `.` or `..` name;
the polled one for `github`.

reviewer.description: The GitHub login whose review requests a `pull_request.review_requested` trigger polls.

teams.description: The GitHub teams, as `org/team`, whose review requests start tasks for `reviewer` too.

timezone.description: The IANA zone `at` is read in, such as `Europe/Paris`; the machine's own when unset.

until.description: When a schedule's day of firings ends; the end of the day when unset.

view.description: The saved Linear view a `linear.view` trigger reads: its id, or the slug id ending its URL.

workflow.description: The workflow a matching event starts, by file name.

title: trigger
